default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-019.title: Floor-pivot touch rejection
E-019.hypothesis: Floor-trader pivots (P, R1/S1, R2/S2 from yesterday's H/L/C) are plotted by most retail platforms, so take-profit and fresh limit orders rest there; a bar that reaches a pivot from one side and closes back on that side shows the resting orders absorbed the push, so trade away from the level.

E-020.title: Range-exhaustion extreme fade
E-020.hypothesis: Once today's range already equals a large share of the 20-session average daily range, day traders' targets are met and fresh momentum buyers are scarce; a new session extreme made then is more likely to be the profit-takers' exit than a new leg, so fade it.

E-021.title: Trend-filtered RSI(2) dip
E-021.hypothesis: Connors-style: inside a trend defined by a long intraday EMA, a 2-period RSI extreme against the trend is short-horizon liquidity selling (or buying) by impatient traders, which trend holders absorb; buy the dip above the EMA, sell the pop below it.

E-022.title: Heavy-volume balance break
E-022.hypothesis: A window that trades much more volume than usual for its time of day while the price stays inside a normal-width range means a large participant is accumulating against passive liquidity; when the range finally breaks, the side that was absorbing has won, so follow the break.

E-023.title: Half-hour mark momentum
E-023.hypothesis: Execution algorithms and discretionary desks re-evaluate on clock marks; at each :00/:30 bar close, a trailing move larger than typical for its horizon means a parent order is still being worked into the next slice, so follow its sign.

E-024.title: High-volume bar level hold
E-024.hypothesis: The midpoint of the most abnormal-volume bar of the last hour or two is where a large participant transacted; when price returns to it and closes back on its side, that participant defends the price (adds or covers), so trade the bounce away from the level.

E-025.title: Consecutive-close run fade
E-025.hypothesis: A run of N consecutive same-direction closes that also covers more ground than usual is driven by short-term chasers and market-order bursts that exhaust the near book; liquidity providers then lean against it, so fade the bar that completes the run.

E-026.title: Busy-session range break
E-026.hypothesis: A session whose cumulative volume is well above normal for the minute is an information day: informed flow is persistent, so a close beyond the recent high/low on such a day is followed by more of the same flow; follow the break only on busy days.

E-027.title: Day-range retracement hold
E-027.hypothesis: After a day leg larger than usual, a pullback to a fixed share (38/50/62%) of the day's range is where missed participants and many retail Fibonacci users place their entries; a bar that reaches it and closes back in the leg's direction resumes the leg.

E-028.title: Quiet-session range fade
E-028.hypothesis: On a session with cumulative volume well below normal for the minute there is no informed flow; a close beyond the recent high/low is noise pushed by small orders into thin books and mean-reverts as market makers re-center, so fade the break only on quiet days.
